newsitem.title: SPAIN: Thousands march in pro-ETA protest in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march in pro-ETA protest in Spain.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Basques took to the streets on Sunday in the largest demonstration by the ETA guerrillas' political wing since the killing of a politician by separatist rebels earlier this month.

With Spain still seething over the murder of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, Basque authorities bolstered security at the pro-ETA march and hundreds of police and private security guards were deployed to maintain order.
The demonstration ended peacefully but sporadic violence later broke out after 30 hooded people clashed with police.

Uniformed police, who had kept a low profile during the march earlier in the day, were deployed onto the streets of the old quarter of the northern Spanish city and fired rubber bullets in the air to disperse the attackers, witnesses said.
Some onlookers emerging from bars shouted "Assassins" and "Get out" as police gathered in groups in the narrow streets weilding guns ready to quell further attacks.

The violence left a sour taste after a peaceful march in which more than 20,000 demonstrators chanted "Independence" and "Long live the ETA military" along the beachfront in San Sebastian, a stronghold of the radical separatist movement.
Herri Batasuna, ETA's political arm, called the protest in response to anti-ETA rallies held across Spain in the past two weeks that drew an estimated six million people.

The Basque regional government had barred a similar demonstration planned for last Saturday because of fears of a possible violent backlash by people outraged by Blanco's killing. But there was no sign of trouble during the march.
Special vans used by anti-riot police were stationed at strategic points, and a police helicopter hovered over the city.
Uniformed officers were kept largely out of sight of protesters, apparently to avoid provoking the kind of clashes that have erupted in the past between police and ETA supporters.
But after the firebomb attack, scores of uniformed police were deployed into the old quarter. Arguments and minor scuffles broke out between ETA sympathisers and opponents.
Shortly afterwards, around 2,000 pro-ETA supporters re-gathered in the centre of the city chanting Herri Batasuna slogans as police watched on.
"This happens every time there's a big Herri Batasuna gathering," one bar owner in the old quarter said. "They come in here and drink and then they look for trouble".

During the demonstration earlier, protesters had waved Basque flags, carried portraits of ETA prisoners and raised clenched fists against a backdrop of San Sebastian's scenic beach. Beachgoers, bicyclists, skaters and joggers continued their activities unfazed by the thousands of noisy protesters.
Herri Batasuna renewed its call for the transfer of some 500 ETA prisoners scattered across the country to prisons in the Basque country of northern Spain.

It was the Spanish government's rejection of a similar demand by ETA that led to Blanco's killing. Guerrillas kidnapped the Basque town councillor from the ruling Popular Party on July 10 and shot him in the head 48 hours later.

Addressing cheering supporters, Herri Batasuna chief spokesman Floren Aoiz accused the government and the news media of conspiring to undermine the separatist movement and said that was tantamount to "throwing gasoline on the fire".
Aoiz reasserted the group's call for talks between the government and ETA, saying Herri Batasuna "is holding out its hand in the search for peace".
The Spanish government has steadfastly refused to negotiate with ETA until it renounces its armed struggle which has so far lead to the deaths of nearly 800 people.
